model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)
model_label: REIT Core AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run on the component engine: revenue x Core FFO margin, less recurring capitalised expenditures (the Core FFO -> Core AFFO bridge) = Core AFFO. Net debt is NOT deducted because Core AFFO is already after interest expense.

historical_growth.eps_basis: Statutory EPS ($6.07 FY2022 -> $3.54 FY2025; $1.24 FY2020) swings on gains on sale and impairments and is not used. The relevant series is Core AFFO/share: 5.69 (FY2022) -> 5.90 (FY2025) = +1.2%/yr over 3 years; 4.13 (FY2020 AFFO) -> 5.90 = +7.4%/yr over 5 years, flattered by the pandemic trough base and the 2021-22 rent spike.
historical_growth.fcf_basis: Core AFFO in $m (the owner-flow analogue for a REIT): 622.1 (FY2022) -> 649.1 (FY2025); 418.2 (FY2020 AFFO) -> 649.1. The 5-year figure includes the 2022 consolidation of the Camden Multifamily Value-Add Funds and equity raised in 2021-22.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Long-run Core AFFO growth set at CPI-like rent growth of 2.5%, consistent with the 3-year Core AFFO/share CAGR (1.2%, depressed by the 2023-26 Sun Belt supply wave) and below the 5-year (7.4%, flattered by the trough base). Book-equity CAGR is not used: it is historical-cost depreciated book, shrinking through depreciation and buybacks, and says nothing about earning power.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-4.3% 3yr / +4.8% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue CAGR (3.4% / 8.6%) and from EPS. Expected for a depreciated-cost REIT with buybacks. Neither series is the anchor; Core AFFO/share and management guidance are.
historical_growth.notes: Core AFFO/share has been flat at ~$5.90 for three years (FY2023-25) as Sun Belt new supply held effective new-lease rates negative (2Q26 new leases -3.3%, renewals +2.8%, blended -0.2%; occupancy 95.7%). FY2026 guidance ($6.75 Core FFO mid) is a ~2% decline in Core FFO/share, driven by lower same-property NOI (guide -0.6% mid), higher overhead and loss of one-off fee income.

scenario_narratives.base: Camden completes its California-to-Sun Belt rebalancing roughly FFO-neutral: run-rate Core AFFO is about $5.72/share on 103.2m FFO-diluted shares, in line with reaffirmed FY2026 Core FFO guidance of $6.75. As Sun Belt deliveries fall away, same-property revenue growth recovers from 0.5% in 2026 to ~3-3.5% in 2028-30 and then fades to CPI-like 2.5%. The Core FFO margin dips on refinancing and the end of development capitalised interest, then recovers to 47.5%. Recurring capex stays at 6.9% of revenue. Core AFFO is capitalised at a 9.5% USD cost of equity with no net-debt deduction.
scenario_narratives.bull: The supply cliff produces a 2011-15-style rent recovery: new-lease rates turn positive in 2027 and revenue grows 4.5-5% at the peak. Recycled capital earns above its ~5% FFO yield, the Core FFO margin rises to 49% on operating leverage and easier refinancing, and a younger portfolio trims recurring capex to 6.7%. Long-run growth is 3.0%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sun Belt oversupply and a regional labour slowdown keep new-lease rates negative through 2027, so same-property revenue is flat in Y2. Refinancing at 5%+ and rising property tax and insurance compress the Core FFO margin to ~44.8%. Rent-stabilisation measures spread to Camden's jurisdictions, recurring capex creeps to 7.2%, and long-run growth settles at 2.0%. Exit at ~13.6x Core AFFO.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Camden is valued as a stream of Core AFFO, which is Core FFO less recurring capitalised expenditures and is the company's own distributable-cash measure. It is capitalised at a 9.5% USD cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because the flow is already after interest. GAAP EPS is set aside: it is dominated by real-estate depreciation and gains on sale. Year 1 is a pro-forma run-rate after the July-2026 California exit and Sun Belt acquisitions, anchored to reaffirmed FY2026 Core FFO guidance. The current price capitalises run-rate Core AFFO at a ~5.8% yield (~17x). That implies about a 9% cost of equity at 3% growth, and a ~7% cap rate on property NOI against the ~5% Camden achieved selling California in July. So the stock sits well below private-market NAV (~$115-128 at a 5.75-6.25% cap) but near what a 5.2% risk-free rate supports on a pure cash-yield basis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: this is a long-duration income stream, so each 50bp on the 9.5% cost of equity moves the base value by roughly 7-8%, and the 10-year Treasury at 5.2% is the dominant input.

The pro-forma revenue base is estimated. Camden does not disclose California revenue separately; the ~$125m estimate uses 3,620 homes at ~1.35x the portfolio's revenue per home, and a +/-$25m error moves Year-1 revenue by ~1.7%. The Year-1 Core FFO anchor comes from guidance, not from that estimate, so the value is less sensitive than revenue.
Sun Belt supply absorption: new-lease rates were still -3.3% in 2Q26. If the 2027 recovery slips a year, the base path converges on the bear path.
Refinancing: $695m of contractual maturities in the next 12 months, $600m of CP at quarter-end, and a new $350m term loan due Jul-2027, all refinancing near 5%.
Regulatory: rent-control and stabilisation legislation, plus the revenue-management class action ($53m settled 2026). Core FFO excludes these costs, but the cash still leaves.
Capital allocation: buybacks at ~$104 in 2026 were above today's price, and redeploying California proceeds at a ~5% FFO yield is at best neutral against a 5.8% AFFO yield on Camden's own stock.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance v8 chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NYSE regular close); 52-week range 96.53-119.81.
data_sources.financials: CPT_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (SEC XBRL: property revenues, net income, OCF, debt, cash, shares, SBC, FY2007-Q2 2026). Core FFO, Core AFFO and recurring capex from Camden earnings releases on EDGAR (CIK 906345): 8-K exhibit 99.1 of 2026-07-30 (Q2-26, guidance), 2026-02-05 (FY2025), 2024-02-01 (FY2023/22) and 2022-02-03 (FY2021/20). Balance sheet, share counts and the California held-for-sale note from the Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-07-31).
data_sources.qualitative: CPT_Analysis.json (2026-09-26): business model, Sun Belt supply cycle, California exit, guidance, risks.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2025 (Dec-25) property revenues, US$m, CPT_Metrics.csv (10-K FY2025; ties to the Q4-25 earnings release: $1,573.5m = $1,399.9m rental + $173.6m non-lease components). Revenue is the DRIVER line only; the flow valued is Core AFFO.
inputs.share_count_basis: FFO-diluted share count (common shares plus OP units convertible into common, the same denominator Camden uses for FFO/Core FFO/Core AFFO per share), estimated at 30-Jun-2026. The Q2-2026 weighted FFO-diluted count was 103.957m against 102.342m basic, so OP units and dilutive awards add ~1.6m. During the quarter Camden bought back 1.43m shares, which puts the period-end basic count at ~101.6m on the weighted-average basis; +1.6m gives 103.2m. (The 10-Q's 100.5m period-end figure excludes shares held in deferred-compensation arrangements, which the weighted counts include.) The count is held FLAT. SBC is already expensed inside Core FFO, so adding dilution would double-count it. Further buybacks ($297.9m left on the authorisation) are NOT assumed, because the AFFO forgone on the capital used would roughly offset them at the current ~5.8% AFFO yield.
inputs.net_debt_note: Deliberately ZERO. Core AFFO comes after net interest expense, so deducting balance-sheet debt as well would charge financing twice (dcf-methods SKILL.md). total_debt and cash are recorded for leverage context only.
inputs.total_debt_note: US$m at 30-Jun-2026 (10-Q; CPT_Metrics.csv Q2 2026). After quarter-end, ~$0.9bn of the $1.625bn California sale proceeds retired revolver and commercial-paper balances, and a $350m term loan due Jul-2027 was drawn. Pro-forma net debt is roughly $3.4-3.6bn before H2 buybacks; the Q3-26 10-Q will confirm.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 Core AFFO, US$m (Q4-25 earnings release, 8-K 2026-02-05): Core FFO $757.225m less recurring capitalised expenditures $108.174m. This is about $5.90 per FFO-diluted share. H1-2026 Core AFFO was $309.9m, or $2.95/share.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 Core FFO, US$m ($6.88/diluted share). Nareit FFO was $744.8m ($6.77). CSV FreeCashFlow is blank because XBRL carries no capex tag here. OCF of $826.6m is a GAAP cash measure, not a distributable-flow measure.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC ($16.96m FY2025, CPT_Metrics.csv from the 10-K cash-flow add-back; about 1.1% of revenue) is expensed in G&A/property expense BEFORE Core FFO, and Camden does not add it back in Core FFO or Core AFFO. It is charged once, in the flow. House and street bases coincide (the REIT convention).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $270.7m. YTD-2026 $422.9m (4.06m shares at an average $104.08), funded partly with California-sale recycling. Not projected.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z NYSE regular close (Yahoo v8 chart meta)
inputs.core_affo_history_note: Sources: Q4 earnings releases (8-K exhibit 99.1) dated 2022-02-03, 2024-02-01 and 2026-02-05. FY2020-21 are 'AFFO', which predates Camden's Core definition. FY2024/FY2025 per-share values are derived as Core AFFO $m / (Core FFO $m / Core FFO per share).
inputs.nav_cross_check: At the current price the market capitalises the post-transaction portfolio at roughly a 7% implied NOI cap rate: equity ~$10.1bn (98.12 x 103.2m) plus pro-forma net debt ~$3.5bn gives EV ~$13.6bn, against pro-forma property NOI of ~$950m (run-rate revenue ~$1,490m x ~64% NOI margin, the FY2025 margin). Camden sold California in July 2026 for $1.625bn, which works out to ~5% on our estimate of that portfolio's NOI (~$125m revenue at ~65% margin), and it bought $645m of Sun Belt assets at a ~5% FFO yield. On a 5.75-6.25% private-market cap, NAV is ~$115-128/share. This is a cross-check only, not a model input. It says the AFFO-at-9.5% model sits well below private-market value, which is the discount a public REIT carries when the 10-year Treasury is at 5.2%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The rate is a USD COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: Core AFFO is post-interest and no net debt is deducted. 10-year UST 5.18% (^TNX, 2026-09-25) + 0.85 beta x 5.0% ERP = 9.4%, used as 9.5%. The beta is below 1 because this is an investment-grade apartment REIT whose housing-demand revenue re-prices annually, with net debt/EBITDA ~5x. The same 9.5% applies in all three scenarios, so scenario risk sits in the flows. That is in line with CCI (9.5%) and below BXP (11.5%, office).
inputs.lease_treatment: Camden's own ground/office leases as lessee are immaterial. They sit in property and G&A expense inside Core FFO and are not separately modelled.
inputs.nci_treatment: The FFO-diluted share count includes the OP units (income allocated to non-controlling interests is added back in FFO), so flow and denominator are on the same basis. No separate NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: Model: REIT Core AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md (REIT row), following the house US-REIT precedent (BXP, CCI) and the ARG.NZ/PCT.NZ/IPL.NZ family. GAAP net income is dominated by real-estate depreciation (~$598m FY2025) and gains on sale ($261m FY2025; about $1bn expected on the 2026 California sale), so neither EPS nor P/E means anything here. Engine mapping: EBITDA margin = Core FFO / revenue (post-interest), D&A = 0 (real-estate D&A is already added back in FFO), capex = recurring capitalised expenditures as % of revenue (the Core FFO -> Core AFFO bridge), SBC = 0 (expensed inside Core FFO), tax = 0 (REIT distributes >=100% of taxable income), WC = 0, net_debt = 0. Development, redevelopment and acquisition capital is NOT deducted: it is growth capital funded from retained AFFO (~26% of AFFO at the $4.24 dividend) plus recycling, and the growth path is held to what that retention can fund. YEAR 1 IS A PRO-FORMA RUN-RATE YEAR, NOT the GAAP FY2026: the July-2026 California exit (11 communities, 3,620 homes, $1.625bn; about $125m/yr of revenue, estimated at 3,620 homes x ~1.35x the portfolio's $26.4k revenue per home) and $645m of Sun Belt acquisitions (2,061 homes, about $43m/yr of revenue at ~$21-22k/home) are annualised on Q2-26 revenue: $392.9m x 4 - 125 + 43 = ~$1,490m, i.e. -5.3% on FY2025. The margin is set so Year-1 Core FFO is about $693m (Q3-26 guidance midpoint $1.69 and the implied Q4 of ~$1.67, x 103.2m shares). That gives Year-1 Core AFFO of about $591m, or $5.72/share, against a FY2026 blended estimate of ~$5.71 (H1 $2.95 + H2 Core FFO $3.36 less ~$0.60 recurring capex). First valuation of this ticker: no prior DCF and no memory entry. FFO/AFFO history comes from EDGAR earnings releases (CIK 906345) because the XBRL-parsed Metrics.csv carries no REIT supplemental measures; it should be backfilled into kpis on a refresh.

bear.growth_rationale: Supply absorption drags into 2027-28 and a Sun Belt labour-market slowdown keeps new-lease rates negative, which pushes same-property revenue to flat in Y2. Rent-control or stabilisation measures spread to Camden's jurisdictions (Analysis JSON: high severity). Long-run growth is 2.0%, below CPI in real terms, as build-to-rent single-family competition caps pricing.
bear.margin_rationale: Pandemic-era low-coupon debt and CP refinance at 5%+ while NOI is flat. Property taxes and Gulf Coast insurance rise faster than rents. The $53m revenue-management settlement shows the legal-cost line can recur, even though Core FFO excludes it.
bear.capex_rationale: Recurring capex drifts up with insurance- and casualty-driven replacement cycles and the ageing Houston/DC core.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 2.0% gives ~13.6x and binds below the 16x cap (a ~7.3% exit AFFO yield).

base.growth_rationale: Y1 is the pro-forma run-rate after the California exit and the Sun Belt acquisitions (see inputs.notes). Y2 is +2.0%: same-property revenue recovers from the 2026 0.5% guide to ~1.5% as Sun Belt deliveries fall sharply from their 2024-25 peak, plus lease-up of the three developments ($492m, 1,162 homes). Y3-Y5 are 3.0-3.5% as the supply cliff lets new-lease rates turn positive. Management reported July signed blends up 160bp sequentially, and 75% of communities were positive. The path then fades to 2.5%, CPI-like rent growth, fundable from the ~26% of AFFO that is retained.
base.margin_rationale: Row = Core FFO / revenue. FY2025 was 48.1%. Year 1 is 46.5% because the California assets left at a ~5% cap while part of the proceeds went to buybacks, which cut shares rather than add FFO dollars. Other drags: FY2026 overhead up ~$0.045/share, one-off fee income of $0.04 lost, and 2026 same-property expenses +2.5% against revenue +0.5%. Y2 dips to 46.3% as capitalised interest on the development pipeline ends and $695m of 12-month maturities plus CP refinance near 5%. The margin then recovers to 47.5% on operating leverage once rent growth outpaces the mostly fixed interest bill. It does not return to 48.1%.
base.capex_rationale: Recurring capitalised expenditures (the Core FFO -> Core AFFO bridge) held at the FY2024/FY2025 actual of 6.9% of revenue ($106.4m / $1,543.8m and $108.2m / $1,573.5m). FY2023 was 6.3% and FY2022 6.4%. The sold California assets were older; the acquired Sun Belt assets average ~5 years old, which argues for a slightly lower ratio, but Gulf Coast insurance, casualty exposure and an ageing core Houston/DC book offset that.
base.tax_rationale: Zero. Camden is a REIT and distributes at least 100% of taxable income by policy (10-Q liquidity section), so Core AFFO is already after tax.
base.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 2.5% gives ~14.6x terminal Core AFFO (a 6.8% AFFO yield) and binds below the 20x cap. Camden has historically traded at ~17-25x Core AFFO; it trades at ~17x today on the $5.72 run-rate.

bull.growth_rationale: The Sun Belt supply cliff (starts down sharply from the 2022-23 peak) produces a rent-growth recovery like 2011-15. New-lease rates turn positive in 2027, and California proceeds are redeployed accretively through the $195m of awarded acquisitions and development starts. Long-run growth is 3.0%, supported by in-migration to Texas, Florida and the Carolinas.
bull.margin_rationale: Operating leverage on rent growth with expense growth held near 3%, and lower refinancing coupons if the 10-year eases from 5.2%. The margin recovers above the FY2025 48.1% to 49%.
bull.capex_rationale: A younger post-recycling portfolio (acquired assets average ~5 years old) runs recurring capex slightly below the FY2025 6.9%.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon at 9.5% / 3.0% gives ~15.8x and binds below the 20x cap. Same cost of equity as base: the bull case is better flows, not a cheaper rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: The house default is 15/50/35. Bear is lifted to 20% and bull trimmed to 30%. Three years of flat Core AFFO/share, FY2026 guidance down ~2%, still-negative new-lease spreads and a 5.2% 10-year Treasury make the downside a live one. It is still not a solvency case: investment-grade balance sheet, ~$0.9bn of debt retired from the California proceeds, 95.7% occupancy, and dividend cover of ~1.35x ($4.24 against ~$5.72 AFFO). The bull weight stays meaningful because Sun Belt construction starts have fallen sharply and July signed blends improved 160bp sequentially.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
